(2) SHACL shapes: the `sh:property` blocks for `domain:hasRationale` (sh:class domain:Rationale) and `domain:supersedes` (sh:class domain:InformationRecord) are removed from `shape:ArchitecturalDecisionShape` and added to `shape:InformationRecordShape`, so SHACL enforcement applies to all subclasses rather than only ArchitecturalDecision. Rationale: domain/range declarations on OWL object properties and SHACL property shapes must match the actual structural invariant — since any InformationRecord can supersede another and carry a Rationale, restricting these to ArchitecturalDecision was ontologically incorrect and caused SHACL conformance failures when these predicates were used on non-decision subjects. These are mechanical follow-ons to the InformationRecord root-class decision (see https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/5e1dae27-324e-490e-ab35-b3f05894f0e6).

title: templates/CLAUDE.md: distributable agent-config template encoding graph-first workflow for MOOSEDev-adopting projects
text:
# templates/CLAUDE.md: distributable agent-config template encoding graph-first workflow for MOOSEDev-adopting projects

Commit 5d688415ad adds templates/CLAUDE.md — a reusable, drop-in CLAUDE.md template for any project that adopts the MOOSEDev MCP server as long-term memory. The template encodes the full graph-first workflow: (1) recall-first (list-all get_relevant_context before non-trivial work; a topic-scoped empty result is not an empty graph); (2) capture as typed records (record_important_decision with appropriate kind, including rationale and rejected alternatives; always report what was written); (3) align before coining new terms (align_concepts / suggest_mappings); (4) correct via supersede_decision or retract_decision — never silently duplicate; (5) validate with validate_against_architecture after capturing. Includes a tool-selection ladder (get_relevant_context → query → sparql, cheap → precise), a capture-kinds cheat sheet (ArchitecturalDecision, Constraint, Requirement, Pattern, AntiPattern, Lesson), and standard engineering practice sections (plan mode, subagent strategy, self-improvement loop targeting the graph, verification, elegance, autonomous bug fixing). README.md directory listing updated to include templates/. Intentionally scoped to workflow instructions for the consuming project — MOOSEDev's own design invariants are NOT copied into the template, keeping it lean. Rationale: consumable projects should not have to reverse-engineer the graph-first discipline from MOOSEDev's own CLAUDE.md; the template is how MOOSEDev propagates correct tool usage to the broader ecosystem of adopting projects.

title: validate_against_architecture: honest SHACL subset — minCount + datatype enforced, all other constraints counted as skipped
text:
# validate_against_architecture: honest SHACL subset — minCount + datatype enforced, all other constraints counted as skipped

Commit bda5f872 (M3 complete, src/validation.rs + src/mcp/mod.rs): on-demand SHACL validation of the project knowledge graph. Deliberately implements only two constraint types: (1) sh:minCount 1 — detects nodes of the target class hierarchy that are missing the required predicate entirely; (2) sh:datatype — detects existing predicate values that are not literals with the shape-declared datatype. All other declared constraints (sh:class, sh:node, sh:in, sh:maxCount, sh:qualifiedValueShape) are counted per property shape and reported as skipped. Node-level sh:or constraints are also counted separately. RDFS subclass traversal is performed inside SPARQL (rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf* property paths) because Oxigraph does not perform RDF inference. Reads shapes from both SE_SHAPES_GRAPH_IRI and ARCH_SHAPES_GRAPH_IRI. ValidationReport always reports shapes_checked, skipped, and violations counts — never implies full SHACL coverage. Exposed as the validate_against_architecture MCP tool. Key design choice: a partial validator that admits its scope is more trustworthy than one that silently ignores constraints (invariant #6: auditability). The module is exposed pub(crate) in lib.rs and format_report() provides a human-readable block for MCP output.
